Permit API: 005-27792
Unconventional: No

Comments: On March 2, 2023, the Department conducted an on site meeting with the Operator, Dave Hilty to evaluate the vegetative cover on site and progress of spill remediation.A stipulated order (No. 2019-1701-CIV) was executed by the Department regarding multiple sites, including this site, on 12/19/2019.The Operator was informed on site that the site has not achieved 70% uniform vegetative cover. The site is currently seeded. The Operator informed the Department that the spill that occurred in the area seen in Photo 3 has been remediated, but the impacted material has not yet been disposed of. The Operator informed the Department that McCutcheon Enterprises was asking for contact from the Department before disposing of the impacted material. The Department requests further detail regarding McCutcheon's request. The Department requests disposal documents and waste manifest for the impacted material when made available to the Operator. The Operator informed the Department that the erosion gully on the northwest side of the site was filled in and seeded (Photo 5). The Department recommended the Operator maintain the silt fence BMP at the top of the access road (Photo 6).Equipment that had previously been staged near the site has been removed (Photo 9).Violation for equipment on site is being corrected. All other violations remain outstanding.

Comments: On 6/07/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at theCessna 1 OG Wellsite, for violations cited on 5/6/2024 (Inspection ID:3757306, Enforcement ID:428752).Violations includedViolations of 102.11(a), 102.4(b)1, 102.22(b)1, 102.22(a), and 78.53.The following was observed:-The access road was not passable by vehicle. Tree clearing and earth disturbance had taken place since the initial site visit (IR3757306). Repairs to the access road had not begun as of the time of inspection (Photos 1-9).-Little temporary stabilization was observed. I recommend adding additional stabilization if work will not resume within four days (Photo 10).-A partially downed tree was observed leaning over a portion of the location of the previous access road (Photo 11).-E and S controls were observed onsite, installed incorrectly. Silt sock was installed over top of the cleared tree debris, allowing for the undermining of potential sediment laden water. An E and S plan could not be located onsite. The Department requests a copy of the E and S Plan be provided, and I recommend that the E and S controls be installed properly and according to the E and S plan (Photos 12-24).Determination:Violations of 102.11(a), 102.4(b)1, and 78.53 remain outstanding.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/08/2026
Comments: The site of this oil spill is in a forested area on an access road south off Center Hill Road, 430 yards on south branch of access. Will Warfel contacted WQS Taylor and reported to National Response Center that there was a release of about 20 gallons of crude oil from a tank the wind tipped over in one of the recent storms. The path of the crude oil was ~320 yards on the access from origin of the spill to low spot where it left the road and seeped into the stream. Blobs of oily material were found ~60 yards downstream. Two absorbent booms were placed in the stream along with absorbent pads. One absorbent boom was placed across the access road and one was positioned along the road to catch any remaining oil from seeping to stream. Visual clean-up of oil and oil contaminated soil completed where the tank tipped and leaked oil. The tank was removed and contaminated soil piled and covered until soil is tested and can be received at a licensed facility.Violations for the release of oil to ground and into a stream issued with this inspection. Clean-up, restoration and stabilization of spill site with vegetation and receipt of tipping receipts and waste manifest by the Department required to lift violations.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions at the site after a release of an estimated 50 barrels of produced fluid occurred on and off of the secondary containment on 3/3/23. I met with company man Dan Ringer upon arriving on location. The frac is complete and most of the equipment for the frac has been removed from the pad. Some of the well site secondary containment used for the frac remains on the pad and will be used for the upcoming drill-out. The pad surface was very dry. No stormwater was observed in any of the stormwater controls. Some fluid with an electrical conductivity of 17.48 mS/cm was observed in one area of the secondary containment near the well heads. This area of the containment did not have a berm at the edge of the containment at the time of this inspection since the equipment for the frac had recently been moved off of the containment. I made the recommendation to the company man to have the fluid vacuumed up right away and he said he would have it taken care of. He also said that the containment berms would be replaced on the same day. No other issues noted.Violations remain outstanding on permit 081-21907 for release to the pad surface from 3/3/23.

These tanks are located along Farm Lane, in Pleasant Township. The complainant was concerned that if a release occurred the gravel and unconsolidated material in the containment would not be sufficient to contain a release.The small upper containment directly around the stock tanks is constructed with a dirt and gravel base and walls, and includes a drain pipe that is directed the into a second containment downslope of the upper containment. The upper containment wall and base material around the tanks consists of gravel and does not appear to comply with the permeability requirements. In its current state the height of the upper containment wall would not be sufficient in containing a substantial release. The lower containment at the bottom of the slope, intended to contain an overflow from the upper containment in the event of a substantial release, is nearly full of water and does not have the capacity required by Chapter 78.64.

Comments: On 11/1/22 a routine complete inspection of the Consol/USX 24 OG Well site was conducted. I was accompanied by Chase Ambrose (PA DEP). During the inspection the following was observed: -A well tag was observed on the wellhead (Photo #1).-The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo #2).-Some corrosion was observed on the well, production equipment, and tank (Photos #3-6).-Gas smell was noticed coming from production equipment (Photo #5)-Holes observed in tank patched with tape, sticks, and screws (Photos #7-9).-Black oily/greasy residue present on gravel inside earthen berm (Photos #10-12).-Water observed beading on oily/greasy residue on tank (Photo #13). -No elevated conductivity was observed. I called Bryan Goletz of Diversified and notified him of the gas smell, the tank, and the grease that was observed inside the tank berm. He informed me that the tank is on the list to be replaced, and he will get out to the well site to address the gas leak and grease. The site is being referred to an OGI for follow-up regarding the gas odor.Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, and 78.54 are being issued for the release and condition of the tank.

Some puddles were cloudy while others appeared to have a sheen to them. Pooling of fluid with sheen were also seen on the secondary containment in some areas.Conductivity readings were taken inside the different spill areas as well as adjacent to the marked spill areas to determine whether any areas outside of these markings were contaminated as well. A background conductivity reading was taken at the well pad perimeter upslope (0.0159 mS) and the rest of the readings are as follows: inside Spill Area 1: 12.6 mS, outside of Spill Area 1: 0.085 mS, inside of Spill Area 3: 1.529 mS, inside of Spill Area 4: 2.05 mS, outside of Spill Area 4: 0.011 mS, from in a cloudy puddle seen in Spill Area 5: Over Range, outside of Spill Area 5: 0.011 mS, inside Spill Area 6: 1.762 mS, from a sheen puddle seen in Spill Area 7: Over range, and lastly 3 readings were taken in stained sediment around the well pad to see if there were other contaminated areas: 0.042 mS, 0.693 mS and 0.0227 mS. In theory, Range believes there to be one or more holes/tears in the secondary containment, but none of them have reportedly been discovered at the time of the inspection. Nick stated that the drill rig has two more weeks on site. During these two weeks as equipment is removed and once the drill rig is gone, Range plans to continue inspecting the secondary containment, specifically in areas that currently have equipment on top of it. Any further releases will continue to be cleaned and any holes/tears will be repaired as they are found. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 2020-03-16
Comments: A routine inspection was conducted to assess overall conditions. A frac is on-going. I met with several Rockdale representatives during this inspection. Both of Rockdale's field technicians accompanied me on this inspection including Jen Compton. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment to hold the produced water for the frac. Two aboveground storage tanks (AST) are also present and store freshwater. The tanks and their containment appear to be in good condition overall. Tarps are being used in the stormwater channels to prevent stormwater or other fluids from entering the northeast infiltration basin. Stormwater continues to pumped from the northeast basin and disposed of. Fluid is collecting in the northeast corner of the pad as it did in August 2019 while drilling was taking place on the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was approximately 2.3 mS/cm. Jen Compton said that she would have the fluid pumped out and that an investigation would be done to determined why the EC appears to be elevated. This is the same area where fluid with elevated conductivity collected while drilling was occurring on the pad. The Department recommends frequent monitoring of this area of the pad. The Department also recommends removing fluid that accumulates in this area of the pad as needed. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.

Comments: On 08/25/2025, a complaint inspection was conducted at the plugged Blum 1 Well Site following receipt of a complaint (CTS 391464). The well was plugged on 12/12/2019. I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Jena Bonasorte (PA DEP).The following was observed:The well appeared to be plugged. A monument with the well's permit number was on location. The permit number on the monument was incorrect and should read 37-125-22119-00. It appears that several pieces of casing remain at the plugging location (Photos 1-3).I observed several spots of oil/grease on the ground around the plugged well and what appears to be a demolished compressor station or dehydration system (Photos 4-9).The well site around the plugged well was not completely restored to original contour and vegetated. The adjacent compressor station was demolished, however equipment was present and piping remained. Pipes and electrical equipment were sticking out of the ground (Photos 2, 10-17).The access road was restored but appears to still be used (Photos 18, 19).The area where production tanks were previously, as seen on aerial imagery, displayed bare dirt (Photos 20-22). The tanks were not noted. Conductivity readings were obtained and no elevated readings were noted.The Department has not received a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator following plugging. I recommend that the WSRR is submitted. Due to the operator failing to submit a WSRR within 60 days after restoration of the well site, failure to restore the site to original conditions, and failure to remove equipment/facilities, violations of 78.65(3), OGA3216(A), and OGA3216(D) are being issued.

Inspection Date: 11/07/2022
Comments: On November 7, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline completed an inspection to follow up with a reported spill of production fluid outside of containment at the EQT ARO LLC Larrys Creek Fish and Game Well Pad C. Rick Hall with EQT reported a spill had occurred on November 3, 2022 at 2000, that a water truck leaked about 10-20 gallons of production fluid while loading. Mr. Hall reported that a clean up crew was scheduled to remove the impacted soil. The area of excavation was about 30 ft. X 15 ft. and only about an inch of soil was scraped up to remove the impacted soil. The impacted soil was placed in a covered roll off dumpster onsite. The DEP screened the area of excavation with a soil conductivity meter and measured 10 uS/cm to 60 uS/cm. The DEP observed some rust and pitting on the production fluid tanks. A hole was also observed in the liner of the secondary containment for the production fluid tanks. The DEP recommends monitoring the production fluid tanks and repairing or replacing the tanks as necessary. The DEP also recommends repairing the hole in the liner of the secondary containment as soon as possible to avoid a inadvertent release. The spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. These violations have been immediately corrected.

Code § 102.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/25/2024
Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
Violation ID: 8185044
Permit API: 125-27410
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024, routine inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources Inc well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on April 1, 2016.The following was observed:Well 10H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 1 and 2). A small amount of grease was observed on the well pad surface below the well head (see photo 3). There are five other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 4). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 5). Additional secondary containment that appeared to be severely deteriorated was observed next to the production tanks (see photo 6). This appears to be used for pump trucks that empty the production tanks. The ERP and PPC plan were onsite (see photos 7 and 8). Deep accelerated erosion rills were observed in multiple portions of the access road, with one of them appearing to empty into a storm culvert (see photos 11-15). The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that any grease or other fluids used during routine maintenance that fall onto the well pad surface are immediately removed. The Department also recommends that deteriorated secondary containments and other onsite equipment are replaced to mitigate the risk of a spill from occurring on site. Finally, the Department recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that contain regulated substances are equipped with secondary containments to mitigate the risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.Violations are being issued against the severely eroded access road.
